title: V10 residual whitelist conflicts with retained extended-format fneg contract
description: Literal normative row in section12.4: "| V10 | an operand or result of type `half`, `bfloat`, `x86_fp80`, `fp128` or `ppc_fp128` other than in `bitcast`, `load`, `store`, `select` and `phi` (after N33) |". New validator-v10-residue follows literal V10 and expects rejection for half fneg, while the checker accepts and the retained-operation contract supports acceptance. Pre-edit hand derivation (2026-10-29): Reading A applies V10 literally. load half and bitcast half are exceptions, but fneg half is not, so validator-v10-residue rejects. title: Indirect calls in device code (R2)
description:
Audit row(s): O-01; also used by B-16, B-22, B-33
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: the call graph has direct-call edges only (§4.1); §8.1 'runs host functions natively'; no lowering for CC, R or lifted code

Rungs blocked: 4, 5, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Candidate sets for every indirect call (C1-C5 generalised; fallback as in B-33). The device closure includes all candidates. Function-address encoding: a function's address is its comparison-link address (D15). Lowering: CC/R use a compare chain or binary search over the encodings, ending in static `call @f_k`; lifted code uses `t = lift.icmp.eq fp c_k; qbranch t ^call_k ^next` with static `lift.call`. Unbounded -> reject (decision 3 analogue).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes, no change: CC `call @f` is static (ISA §4.1); `lift.call @f` is static and `qjumpr` is intra-function (ISA §4.2). Compare-and-branch is the mechanism; an indirect-call instruction would be efficiency only.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §0, §3.1 taint row, §3.2 (functions are placed by a driver-controlled comparison link whose link map the device loader replicates). Rung 4: SQLite VFS, pcache, mutex, function tables; rung 5: Julia `jl_fptr_*`; rungs 6, 7: kernel ops tables. Plan risk R2. Top-ten narrowing #4.

description:
Audit row(s): D21, B-32 (also D3, D11(b) share the redesign)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D21 'one input register; producers pack inputs into it'; §6.1, §6.6 BD-E-REGION-TYPE: oracle candidates must be iT (iN), 1 <= N, T <= 128

Rungs blocked: 1, 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): New oracle marker `__bennett_oracle_i(f, budget, iface)`, where `iface` points to a descriptor of handles (inputs, target, fault, mem regions) and classical args (provenance handles it like a table). Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §4.2 (inputs preserved), NS §8 rung 4 (rowid plus database), 7 (syscall args plus snapshot), 8. Rung 1: multi-argument functions need a packing wrapper. Top-ten narrowing #2.

description:
Audit row(s): D11, B-17 (N half), B-51; marker list of §3.2 has no effect markers
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D11 'F(8)'; §4.3/N18/V12; §8.6 'no external effect in 0.1'

Rungs blocked: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): (a) R tier: reserved runtime primitives `__bennett_dev_<model>_<op>` (or effect markers) that the plugin lowers to ISA `effect model.op`; `bennett-runtimes` musl and Julia shims implement their syscall layers on them. (c) An effect with no model stays F(8) and a `trapped` coverage line: that part is L (NS §3.3).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: R tier ISA §7.3 (console, clock, entropy, block), §4.1 `effect`; coherent tier ISA §7.2 interface regions, §3.7 pseudo-locations; host calls ISA §10 `hostcall`. New device models: ISA §17 item 3 (ISA change only for models beyond the four).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 effects row (marker calls on the device side for console, clock, entropy, block device), §4.2 effects table, §5 (kernel boots on the VM in the reversible tier with its devices modelled). title: Full lifted subset in oracle regions: memory, calls, floating point, vectors (BD-E-LIFT-SUBSET)
description:
Audit row(s): D4, B-39 (and B-45 -> D16)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D4; §9.1 'Lifting of memory, calls, floating point and vectors in oracle regions'; §6.4.3

Rungs blocked: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): Full lifted subset. loads, stores and GEPs -> `lift.boundscheck`/`lift.load`/`lift.store` (<= 128-bit pieces). Globals -> layout globals and data images; `lift.addr`. Escaping allocas -> `lift.alloc` at entry and `lift.free` at exit, or a shadow-stack global; non-escaping allocas -> locations. Allocator shim malloc/free -> `lift.alloc`/`lift.free`. Direct calls -> `lift.call`/`lift.ret` lprocs. Indirect calls -> O-01. FP -> soft-float bitcode from `bennett-arith`, lifted like any code. Vectors -> scalarisation before mapping (a normaliser rule). First-class aggregates -> per-field locations. Integers wider than 128 bits -> legalised into <= 128-bit limbs. Intrinsics: `*.with.overflow`, `*.sat`, bswap, ctpop, fshl/fshr, bitreverse, memcpy/memmove/memset -> expansions or runtime lprocs. Varargs -> O-03. Unwinding -> D10 transform. Pre-flight checks need the phase-1 interpreter.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §4.2 rows `lift.load/store/alloc/free/call/ret/addr/boundscheck`; §3.7 stack and locations; §7.2 lifted memory; §16.3 example 2. Wide payloads: G-15.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 ('The ordinary loads and stores of lifted classical code (all of SQLite's) ... are lifted coherently'), §3.2 (soft-float; object-bounds model). Rung 1 only partially: any call left after O3 (Rust panic paths for / and %, Julia throw paths, non-inlined helpers) is outside the subset. Top-ten narrowing #1.

title: Kernel and runtime platform: MMIO, interrupts, privileged state, context switch, exec, setjmp/longjmp
description:
Audit row(s): O-06 (G-16 is the efficient ISA alternative)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: volatile accesses to device addresses become plain accesses by N9 and then memfault; no interrupts, address translation, stack switching, exec of user programs, setjmp/longjmp

Rungs blocked: 5, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Needs a phase-2-style spike. Mechanisms without an ISA change: MMIO by address-range shims onto device models; interrupts by polling at loop back edges and function entries (deterministic timer from the clock model); context switch and setjmp/longjmp by an Asyncify-style transform (frames spilled to memory and rewound); user programs compiled as device code with a soft-MMU instrumentation of their loads and stores. Efficient alternative: ISA gap G-16.

ISA 0.8 support: Without G-16: yes, at large cost.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §5 (boots on the VM with its devices modelled, un-boots to the reset vector), §8 rungs 5/6/7; NS §9.11 lists setjmp as open, not excluded. Rung 6: all; rung 7: non-local exit from `panic()` to make the panic flag the payload; rung 5: Julia exceptions use sigsetjmp.

title: Taint-driven lifting of classical code under ctrl/adj/compute (coherent lifting; R1)
description:
Audit row(s): 1.4-d, D17, B-31, B-50, O-05 (all same mechanism); audit §3 TDL-1..TDL-10
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §1.4(d), §6.1 'region kind fixed by the marker', §6.6 'plugin never outlines', §8.4 (classical code of ctrl/adj/compute bodies runs once, classically), §14 D17

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): see audit

ISA 0.8 support: Not a dedicated ISA change. Yes: ISA §5.3 (action bodies call oracles), §4.7 `ctl w <call>` and `(args..)`, §3.3 region binding, §5.2 oracle is an involution. Efficiency items: G-13, G-14, G-15.

Why it is a narrowing / context: Does not block rungs 4/7/8 (they use the explicit `oracle` marker once D4, D21/D3, D11, B-42, O-01 are removed). Blocks NS §0 ('controlled-anything ... everything else is inferred') and the NS §5 REPL scene `when(q) do f(x) end`. Under the draft, classical stores of a ctrl body happen on both branches of q: a different result, not just a rejection. O-05 (coherent memory after a region) is part of this (TDL-4, TDL-2).


Taint-driven lifting (TDL), specifiable as dialect 0.2 rules (audit §3.2; ISA 0.8 permits it, no ISA change needed):
- TDL-1 Interface vs body. The marker fixes the region's interface (action for ctrl/adj/compute, oracle for oracle/inplace). The body is partitioned by content (TDL-3), never rejected for containing classical code (NS §4.2).
- TDL-2 Coherence lattice Cl below Co over values and (field-sensitive) abstract objects, flow-sensitive. Seeds: a store during generation of an action region to an object live after the invocation makes it Co from region exit (promotion); a load from a Co object is Co. Propagation: data dependence; control dependence (Co branch makes dependents Co, stores predicated); memory (store of Co value or under Co control makes the object Co). Interprocedural, context-sensitive, polyvariant clones per coherence signature (NS §3.1).
- TDL-3 Partition. G (generation) = Cl instructions not control-dependent on a Co branch whose stores target Cl or non-escaping objects; runs once in CC as today. Each maximal single-entry single-exit region of Co instructions is outlined (CodeExtractor) into O_k: Cl live-ins become classical args, Co live-ins input registers, Co objects read the arena region (in), Co live-outs and written bytes output targets. O_k is lifted by the D4 map; irreducible coherent code is outlined as a whole function.
- TDL-4 Coherent arena: every object that may become Co is allocated in a static range [A_coh, A_coh+2^A) of the layout, inside every oracle's [0,2^H) and disjoint from CC globals/heap (ISA §7.1/§7.2; G-13 would lift the restriction); contents in a CC-held qreg[8*2^A] bound to region[A,8] (ISA §3.3). The bennett-runtimes coherent allocator keeps bookkeeping classically; a still-Cl arena object has a CC shadow, G-code stores mirrored as basis-state updates. After promotion, CC reads of the object are a compile-time error BD-E-TAINT-HOST (host-visible outputs leave only through measurement).
- TDL-5 Events. Case A: a G store to an escaping object with classical old and new contents appends `xmask o, old^new`. Case B: each dynamic entry into slice O_k appends `oracle O_k` (args = Cl live-ins, ins = Co live-in registers, mem = arena, tgt = fresh registers for Co live-outs and new byte contents, fr = fresh wire[4]) then exchange events (`qexch` on slices for classical addresses, `qexchm` for Co addresses, ISA §4.6). Outputs wider than 128 bits are sliced (G-15).
- TDL-6 Control and adjoint: ctrl adds the control wire to every event (`ctl w`, ISA §4.7); oracle_call, qexch, qexchm and X are self-adjoint (ISA §5.3). adj of a region with escaping writes consumes the history registers of its forward invocation; without them the adjoint of a non-injective update does not exist (that case is L: NS §4.2 requires an action to be a unitary on its declared wires).
- TDL-7 History: displaced contents, per-slice fault wires, Co temporaries; lives in declared mutable wires; freed when the scheduler chooses (NS §3.1 garbage row); `compute(f, use)` frees it through adjoint(E_f). Memory is versioned, never overwritten.
- TDL-8 Faults: a final combine oracle XORs the first nonzero per-slice code into the region's declared fault register (lifted select chain).
- TDL-9 Budget: the ctrl operand or the D2 table gives (steps, heap, stack, depth) for every O_k token; exhaustion is that slice's FAULT_BUDGET_* reaching the region fault.
- TDL-10 Co control of quantum operations: a marker call control-dependent on a Co branch or with Co index/op code: an oracle computes the condition into a fresh wire and the gate is issued under `qpred` once per candidate (ISA §3.5, §4.6). A Co angle is predicated per candidate when finite, else rejected (L: NS promises predication, not superposed parameters). A Co trip count of a gate-issuing loop is padded to the budget bound, unrolled in the event list, per-iteration flags kept as history; G-14 would replace that with an action step machine.

ISA gaps: G-13 (dynamic region base), G-14 (action step machine), G-15 (wide oracle payloads) are efficiency items for ISA 0.9. ISA-4 matters for adj of a generation whose register set is known only at run time (record the event trace with its registers and replay in reverse). R1 is a dialect design task for phase 3 with no ISA blocker.
